key_insight: A periodic octagonal core raises a composite sandwich panel’s transition frequency by up to 70% relative to honeycomb cores while reducing modal density.
engineering_relevance: Core geometry offers a route to delay the onset of increased modal density and acoustic radiation without changing the reported mass-to-stiffness ratio.
method: Model a periodic core unit cell with 3D finite elements.
Use the wave/finite element method to compute dispersion without Gibson–Ashby core homogenisation.
Compare core geometries through transition frequency and modal density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons of cellular cores sharing the same mass-to-stiffness ratio, with the octagonal design achieving up to a 70% transition-frequency increase.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or quantify acoustic-radiation reductions, so these remain to be established.
paper_title: Vibro-acoustic optimisation of sandwich panels using the wave/finite element method
